subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

options: It has delocalised electrons between layers
Each carbon bonds to four others
questions.explain: In graphite each carbon bonds to three others, leaving delocalised electrons that carry charge.

questions.q: Why is cryolite added to the aluminium oxide during the electrolysis of aluminium?
options: To make oxygen at the cathode
To lower the melting point and save energy
questions.explain: Cryolite lowers the melting point of aluminium oxide, reducing the energy needed.

questions.q: Which scientist proposed that electrons orbit the nucleus in fixed energy shells?
questions.explain: Bohr suggested electrons occupy fixed shells (energy levels) around the nucleus.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of an exothermic process?
options: Neutralisation of an acid and alkali
questions.explain: Neutralisation releases energy, so the temperature of the mixture rises — it is exothermic.

questions.q: Approximately how many particles are in one mole of a substance (Avogadro's constant)?
What is the formula of the compound formed from Mg²⁺ and Cl⁻ ions?
questions.explain: Two Cl⁻ ions balance one Mg²⁺ ion, giving MgCl2.

questions.q: How many moles are in 80 g of NaOH? (Mr = 40)
When citric acid reacts with sodium hydrogencarbonate, the temperature falls. This reaction is:
questions.explain: The temperature drop shows energy is taken in, so the reaction is endothermic.

questions.q: What is the relative charge of a proton?
questions.explain: Protons carry a relative charge of +1.

questions.q: In which state are particles most closely packed and only able to vibrate in fixed positions?
questions.explain: In a solid, particles are tightly packed in a regular arrangement and only vibrate.

questions.q: An atom of sodium has 11 protons and 12 neutrons. How many electrons does it have?
questions.explain: A neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons, so 11 electrons.

questions.q: How does a catalyst speed up a reaction?
options: It increases the concentration of reactants
It provides an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy
questions.explain: Catalysts provide an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.
